turn.question: What should the office check on the signed note before submitting it?

response.answer:
Before submitting the signed office note for N-101, the office should check: 
- The note is the requested document for ALD-1042/N-101. 
- All pages are present and in the correct order (including the signature page) and the signature page belongs to that same note. 
- Page edges are not cropped and the entire text is readable (scan legibility). 
- If using a cover/routing sheet, it is included for routing but does not replace any missing page or signature. 
- The submission references the case/request (ALD-1042 / N-101) and is sent via the office’s established secure document channel. 
- If more than one note/version could match the request, confirm which document the receiving team needs before submitting. 

Also note: the pack requires a signature page but does not define which electronic-signature formats or countersignature arrangements are accepted; those acceptance questions must be clarified with the receiving team if relevant.

turn.question: The office says the note was sent, but the receiving team cannot find it. How should we reconcile that?

response.answer:
Follow these reconciliation steps: 

1) Ask the office for its reported transmission details: time sent, channel used, and any transmission or tracking reference. Label those as office-reported details. 
2) Ask the receiving team to re-check routing and document association using the case/request identifiers (ALD-1042 / N-101). Confirm they searched the correct secure route and looked for the signed note plus its signature page. 
3) Compare the office’s transmission report to the submitted-package inventory and the receiving-team acknowledgments; confirm exactly which document/version each side means. An office report that a note was sent is evidence but does not by itself prove the receiving record or completeness. 
4) If resubmission is needed, have the office send the complete signed note through its established secure document channel, reference ALD-1042 / N-101, and label the file as a replacement so the receiving team can reconcile duplicates. 
5) After the office reports it has sent the document, check for a receiving-team acknowledgment; only that acknowledgment confirms the receiving-team located the signed note (and then a completeness check follows). 

If disagreement persists, request clarification from the receiving support team so both sides agree which document/version to locate or replace.
suggestedFollowups: Ask the office to provide the transmission reference and exact filename they sent for ALD-1042 / N-101.
Request the receiving team to confirm whether a replacement-labeled file will be accepted and how they will acknowledge receipt.

workProduct.subject: ALD-1042 briefing: open N-101 (signed office note) — actions and open questions
workProduct.body:
Snapshot and evidence
- Case: ALD-1042; submitted package PKG-1042; open request N-101 for the signed office note. The package inventory lists a cover sheet, demographic form and an unsigned office note. No payer decision is recorded.
- N-101 specifically requires the signed office note and its signature page; a cover sheet or unsigned note does not satisfy the request.

Objective and immediate blocker
- Objective: help the office supply the exact item requested in N-101 and obtain a clear receiving-team record.
- Immediate blocker: the signed office note and signature page are missing from the receiving-team record; an unsigned note in the package does not satisfy N-101.

Facts to record or confirm in the next office conversation
1) Can the office obtain and provide the complete signed office note and its signature page? (Confirm that the signature page belongs to that same note.)
2) If the office already reported sending the note, obtain their reported transmission details: time sent, channel used, and any transmission or tracking reference. Label these as office-reported details.
3) Which file/version did the office send (file name, creation date, clinician name) so both sides can confirm they’re looking for the same document?
4) Confirm the secure channel the office used and that the office will use its established secure document channel for any resubmission.

Reconciliation / next administrative steps to propose
- Ask the office to resend the complete signed note (with signature page) through the established secure document channel and explicitly reference ALD-1042 / N-101 in the submission and filename.
- When the office reports it has sent the document, request the receiving-team acknowledgment (this acknowledgment is required to confirm the receiving team located the signed note; a transmission reference alone is not the receiving-team confirmation).

What a later update must include
- Office-reported submission details (time/channel/reference) if reported.
- Receiving-team acknowledgment that they located the signed note.
- Receiving-team completeness review that confirms the signature page and document satisfy N-101.
- Any payer decision would be recorded separately (none is recorded now).

Open questions for the office (explicit to ask)
- Can you provide the complete signed note and signature page now? If not, when will it be available?
- If you already sent it, what exact transmission details can you share (time, channel, tracking/reference, file name)?
- Which document/version did you mean to send (so receiving team and office can reconcile duplicates)?

Notes and limits
- Do not place patient records in ordinary email; use the office’s secure document channel. The Knowledge Pack does not supply an upload URL or fax number. A generated email or Pathway note cannot itself create a receiving-team acknowledgment or completeness review.

Prepared by: Avery Chen (HCP office access coordinator) — for administrative follow-up on ALD-1042 / N-101

turn.question: What should we record and check when a benefit-verification response comes back?

response.answer:
Record each returned item exactly as provided and verify its applicability before using it in case guidance. At minimum:  
- Record the response source, response date, and any reference or confirmation number.  
- Associate the response with case ACC-2086 and the intended plan/member identity (preserve the original records and source dates).  
- Record the plan identity, scope of the inquiry and exactly which questions the response answers; keep any unanswered fields marked "unknown."  
- Confirm the response applies to the intended plan, member, requested service and relevant date (do not present an old result or a result for a different service as current for ACC-2086).  
- If wording is ambiguous or scope is unclear, ask the benefit‑verification team or payer to clarify rather than generalize.  
- Do not treat a returned verification as a coverage approval; document that it is a returned benefit result and note next administrative steps.
suggestedFollowups: Ask the benefit-verification team to confirm whether the returned result covers the requested service date and PA requirements for ACC-2086.
If the payer response is ambiguous, request a documented clarification from the payer and a summary of which specific questions remain open.

passages.title: Benefit-verification troubleshooting and routing
passages.section: A readable card still does not resolve the inquiry
passages.text: If a corrected card remains unusable or the inquiry returns a mismatch, compare the specific discrepancy with the office’s confirmed information and ask the benefit-verification team to investigate. A mismatch does not by itself establish that the patient is uninsured or that a service is excluded. Record the returned wording and the question needing resolution. Do not create a replacement identifier or claim that an unsuccessful inquiry is a payer denial.

turn.question: Which facts and unknowns belong in the ACC-2086 access briefing?

response.answer:
Include the following in the ACC-2086 access briefing.

Known facts (record exactly as provided):
- The benefit-verification inquiry is blocked because the Juniper Plan member identifier on the submitted insurance card is unreadable.  
- The office reported the image is blurry and said it can check the member number or send a clearer copy via its secure channel.  
- Prescriber details and the demographic form are on file.  
- No corrected identifier or legible new card has been received.  
- No benefit result, prior-authorization submission, or payer decision is recorded for ACC-2086.

Open questions / unknowns to keep visible (do not fill from other cases or assumptions):
- Whether corrected member information will be received and when.  
- Whether the member has active benefits for the requested service.  
- Whether a prior-authorization is required for this case.  
- Estimated patient cost or patient-responsibility amounts.  
- Which network specialty pharmacy (if any) applies.  
- The eventual coverage outcome (approval/denial/other payer determination).

Record-keeping note: preserve the source and date for each record and keep any unanswered fields explicitly marked as unknown until a documented payer response or corrected input is recorded.
suggestedFollowups: Ask the office to confirm the correct member identifier or provide a legible card image referencing ACC-2086.
Request notification and the payer’s returned benefit record (with source and date) once the benefit-verification team receives a usable member identifier.
